metadata.description: Active negative pair. Paper006 (Zhang-Duchi-Wainwright 2013) studies communication-efficient distributed M-estimation via averaging methods (AVGM, SAVGM, SGDAVGM); the contributions are statistical risk bounds of the form $\sigma^2/(nm) + O(n^{-2})$ for averaged local empirical minimizers under smoothness/strong-convexity, plus bias-corrected and SGD variants. Paper011 (Andoni-Indyk-Nguyen-Razenshteyn 2014) studies $(c,r)$-approximate near-neighbor data structures in $\ell_2^d$ via locality-sensitive hashing, contributing a Gaussian LSH on the sphere and a two-level data-aware ball-carving + Gaussian-LSH scheme that bypasses the $\rho \ge 1/c$ LSH lower bound to achieve $\rho \le 7/(8c^2)$. The two papers share no mathematical objects: paper006's universe is Hessians, Fisher information, $M$-estimator Taylor expansions, and Rosenthal moment inequalities; paper011's universe is hash families, collision probabilities, $(r_1,r_2,p_1,p_2)$-sensitivity, Gaussian-cap partitions, and JL dimension reduction. The only superficial overlap is the meta-level theme of 'scaling computation to large data', which is not a mathematical correspondence. All Level-1 paper-origin nodes on each side are unmatched and emitted as `none` (grouped by category for readability).

matches.explanation: Paper006's definitions are statistical-optimization objects: population risk $F_0(\theta) = \E_\statprob[f(\theta;X)]$, local empirical objective $F_{1,i}$ on machine $i$, asymptotic variance $\sigma^2 = \E[\|H^{-1}\nabla f(\theta^*;X)\|^2]$, and good events controlling Hessian/gradient deviation around $\theta^*$. None of these notions (population minimizer, empirical risk, asymptotic variance, Hessian concentration events) appear in paper011's hashing/ANN setup.

Paper011's paper-original definitions are the $(c,r)$-approximate near-neighbor problem itself and the tensor-power $\mathcal{H}^{\otimes k}$ of a hash family. Neither has any analogue in paper006: paper006 has no metric-space ANN problem, no hash families, and no notion of collision probability under random hashes.

ERM ($\hat\theta = \arg\min_\theta \frac{1}{|S|}\sum_x f(\theta;x)$) is the foundational statistical-learning problem of paper006. Paper011 contains no optimization problem; its core problem (ANN, captured in DP11.1) is a metric-space data-structure problem with no loss function or population risk.

The single/limited-round distributed statistical-optimization problem on $m$ machines is paper006's central focus. Paper011 has no notion of multiple machines, communication rounds, or sample-split estimation.
The Tencent click-through-rate logistic regression application is paper006-specific. Paper011 has no machine-learning application.

Paper006's assumptions are statistical-regularity conditions: compact convex parameter space, local strong convexity of $F_0$ at $\theta^*$, eighth-moment gradient/Hessian bounds with Lipschitz Hessian, third-derivative Lipschitz, and a global smoothness/strong-convexity variant for SGD. Paper011 has no risk function, no $\theta^*$, and no smoothness/strong-convexity hypotheses; its assumptions are about hash-family parameters $(r_1,r_2,p_1,p_2)$ and metric-space structure.

Paper006's algorithms (AVGM, SAVGM, SGDAVGM, two-stage SGD+GD) all aggregate local M-estimators across machines to estimate $\theta^*$. Paper011's algorithms (Gaussian partitioning of a sphere, two-level ball-carving + Gaussian-LSH data structure) build randomized partitions/hashes for ANN queries. The two algorithm families share no input/output type: paper006's algorithms output a parameter vector $\hat\theta \in \R^d$ minimizing a population risk; paper011's algorithms preprocess a point set $P$ and answer near-neighbor queries. Even the cross-algorithm primitive `AP6.4` (SGD warm-up + GD) is unrelated to AP11.1/AP11.2. No meaningful pairwise alignment is possible.

Paper006's equation (projected SGD update $\theta^{t+1/2} = \theta^t - \eta_t \nabla f(\theta^t;X_t)$) is an optimization update rule; paper011's equations specify hashing-data-structure parameters $T$, $k$, $\widetilde{k}_l$ (number of shells, outer/inner hash lengths). No correspondence between gradient updates and hash-length parameter choices.

Paper006's main theorems bound the mean-squared error $\E[\|\hat\theta - \theta^*\|^2]$ of distributed averaging estimators (TP6.1 AVGM: $\sigma^2/(nm) + O(n^{-2})$; TP6.2 SAVGM: bias reduced to $O(n^{-3})$; TP6.3 SGDAVGM: $O(1/(nm)) + O(n^{-3/2})$ via averaged SGD). Paper011's main theorems bound the LSH exponent $\rho = \ln(1/p_1)/\ln(1/p_2)$ for Gaussian LSH on a sphere (TP11.5: $\rho = (1-1/(4\eta^2))/c^2$), its non-idealized shell variant (TP11.6), and the data-aware two-level ANN structure (TP11.7: $\rho \le 7/(8c^2)$). Statistical risk bounds and hashing-exponent bounds do not align; the technical machinery (Taylor expansion + Rosenthal vs. Gaussian-cap collision-probability calculus) is entirely disjoint.

Paper006's corollaries (norm-based AVGM bound; Fisher-information form of AVGM matching the Hájek-Le Cam minimax lower bound up to a factor of 2) are statistical: trace of inverse Fisher information versus inverse-Hessian-weighted gradient variance. Paper011's corollary (CP11.2) transfers the $\ell_2$ result to $\ell_1$/Hamming, achieving $\rho \le 7/(8c)$ via the $\ell_1$-to-$\ell_2^2$ embedding. Statistical efficiency bounds and metric-space ANN exponents have no shared content.

Paper006's paper-original lemmas are technical building blocks for the M-estimator MSE proofs: good-events closeness of $	heta_1$ to $	heta^*$, moment bounds on $
abla F_1(	heta^*)$ and $
abla^2 F_1(	heta^*) - 
abla^2 F_0(	heta^*)$, higher-order moment bounds on $	heta_1 - 	heta^*$, bias/variance bounds for the SAVGM combination, and third-order Taylor expansions of the empirical-minimizer error. Paper011 has no $M$-estimator, no Hessian-deviation moments, and no Taylor-of-the-gradient-equation argument.

Paper011's paper-original lemmas are LSH-specific: tensor-power amplification, Gaussian-cap collision-probability upper/lower bounds, closed-form $\ln(1/p)$ in terms of $\tan^2(\alpha/2)$, distance-after-normalization identity for the shell construction, geometry of bucket decomposition into shells, disjunction-probability inequality, and the chain of $\Pr[\mathcal{A}], \Pr[\mathcal{B}\mid\mathcal{A}], \Pr[\mathcal{C}\mid\mathcal{A}\wedge\mathcal{B}\wedge\neg\mathcal{D}]$ bounds for the two-level analysis. None of these objects (random Gaussian halfspace caps on $S^{d-1}$, smallest-enclosing-ball geometry, hash-event probabilities) have any analogue in paper006.

Proof techniques are entirely disjoint. Paper006's proofs use independence + Taylor expansion of $\nabla F_1$ around $\theta^*$ + vector/matrix Rosenthal-type moment inequalities (de Acosta; Chen-Gittens-Tropp) to control bias and variance of the averaged $M$-estimator. Paper011's proofs combine Gaussian-tail estimates with cap-geometry calculations, JL dimension reduction, Jung's theorem on smallest enclosing balls, and union/Markov bounds over hash collisions. The only generic shared tools (Markov inequality, union bound, Cauchy-Schwarz) are external library lemmas not extracted as paper-original lemmas, so they generate no paper-origin matches.

Paper006's open problems (multi-subsample / with-replacement variants of SAVGM; bootstrap correction for SGDAVGM; extension to non-parametric estimation) are all internal to its averaging-estimator program. Paper011 records no open problems and has no resampling/non-parametric-estimation context.
